question: Harappan cities had a ________ grid pattern of layout with roads that cut each other at right angles.
solution: The correct answer is __**rectangular**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The layout of **Harappan cities** followed a well-planned **rectangular grid pattern**, indicative of their advanced urban planning and engineering skills. • The streets of these cities were designed to **intersect at right angles**, creating a grid-like structure that was highly organized and systematic. • The cities were divided into blocks or sectors, which were further classified into residential, commercial, and administrative zones—an early example of urban zoning. • Drainage systems were meticulously planned, with covered drains running beneath the streets, further supporting the organized layout of the grid pattern. • This system of city planning is evident in major Harappan cities such as **Mohenjo-Daro, Harappa, Kalibangan, and Lothal**.
